steps.prompt: Before the check: what are the five parts of a five-paragraph essay? Write them from memory.

cards.title: Essay foundations: quick review
cards.body: Introduction (hook + thesis), three body paragraphs (one point each, with evidence), conclusion (thesis in new words + a final thought). Argumentative essays convince, informative essays explain, narrative essays tell a true story with a point. Brainstorm both sides, choose what you can prove, then outline.

cards.title: An informative outline
cards.body: An informative thesis names the topic and its parts (“… in three ways”). Each body point explains one part, and the evidence is a fact or example about it. No side to take, so no counterclaim.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll outline an informative essay. Quill gives it a score.

prompts: Look at your outline map. Is every part in place?
Which kind of essay (argumentative, informative or narrative) do you want to write first? Why?
